title: Lesson 51: Mobile Architecture: Offline Support, Sync Strategy, and Mobile Security
description: How to design for the least reliable computer in the architecture: offline support, the sync strategy that gets local changes back without losing work, and the mobile security controls that protect data on a device you do not control.

questions.question: A team needs basic offline record viewing and simple data entry for internal users, with no custom development. Which approach fits?
options: The Mobile SDK, because any offline capability demands custom development
The standard app with Briefcase, configured declaratively by an admin
A fully disconnected app that never syncs with the server
Cloud-only storage that keeps no data on the device at all
questions.explanation: For internal users following standard record workflows, the standard app with Briefcase covers offline viewing and simple entry declaratively, with no development. The Mobile SDK path is reserved for complex offline workflows, hardware integration, or a custom consumer experience.

questions.question: A device syncs a local edit up while the server holds a newer change to the same record. Which pairing keeps the server authoritative without clobbering either change?
options: Overwrite for sync down and leave-if-changed for sync up
Overwrite for sync up and leave-if-changed for sync down
Overwrite for both sync down and sync up
Leave-if-changed for both sync down and sync up
questions.explanation: Using overwrite for sync down lets server data replace the local copy, while leave-if-changed for sync up preserves a local edit rather than clobbering a newer server change. That pairing keeps the server the single source of truth.

questions.question: A device holding offline customer data is lost. Which set of controls limits the damage?
options: A larger local cache so the data survives the loss
Storing a plaintext password so the user can log back in without delay
Encryption at rest, a device passcode, and a remote wipe
Relying on the phone's default settings to protect the app data
questions.explanation: Encryption at rest keeps the data unreadable without the key, a device passcode keeps that key from being trivially accessible, and device management lets the company remotely wipe the app's data when a device is lost.
